# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 58 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_058_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 58

**1** Jesus said: "Blessed is the person who has suffered and has found life."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** EMET and PNEUMA favor "suffered"; LOGOS favors "labored." The Coptic *moka* encompasses both toil and distress; "suffered" is slightly more common in scholarly translations (Lambdin, Patterson) and is adopted here.

**"Suffered"** — the two-clause structure (suffering then finding life) is preserved without elaboration. The brevity is the saying's force.

**"Found life"** — the verb "found" (*he*) connects this beatitude to the seeking-finding chain of the gospel (Sayings 2, 92, 94). Life is not given but found through suffering.

**Synoptic Parallels:** This saying may function as the Thomas counterpart to beatitudes in Q tradition (Matt 5:3-12; Luke 6:20-23), but with an inward, experiential focus rather than ethical instruction. Cf. also James 1:12 ("Blessed is the one who endures trial").
